title: Taper the back of a training head with a clipper over a comb, without shaving it bare
instruction: Taper the back of the training head with the clipper over the comb: the bottom row of hair 8 mm, then 12 mm, 16 mm and 22 mm up to the top row. Then put the comb and the clipper back where they were.
context: Barbers and hairstylists (O*NET 39-5011.00, 39-5012.00; 670,800 US jobs, BLS 2025) cut hair with clippers and combs. To taper with clipper over comb, one hand holds the comb flat in the hair at the distance from the scalp that sets the length; the other runs the clipper along its back. The comb must follow the head's curve, and hair cut too short can't be put back. Unlike TK-CXPYGC's hedge shears, no blade opens: the other hand sets the length.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them (left positive); heights above the table. (1) A barber's vinyl training head on a steel clamp stand, fixed, its axis 40 cm forward on the centre line, facing away from the arms so its back is toward them: a black stand foot 14 cm across, a neck 7 cm across up to 2.8 cm, then the head, covered in short brown hair with a vinyl face on the far side; in simulation as horizontal bands: 14.4 cm across to 4 cm, 16.4 cm to 6.5 cm, 17.2 cm to 9 cm, 17.8 cm to 11.5 cm, 17.6 cm to 14 cm, 16 cm to 16.2 cm and 12.4 cm to 18 cm; a vinyl ear pad (3 cm front to back, 5 cm tall, 8 mm thick, from 6.5 to 11.5 cm high) on each side, centred 9.4 cm from the axis. (2) On the back of the head, twelve locks of brown human hair, each about 6 mm across and 35 mm long, hanging down from their roots: four rows at heights 5.25, 7.75, 10.25 and 12.75 cm, three per row at 20 degrees to the right, straight back, and 20 degrees to the left. (3) A grey rubber mat 3 mm thick, 14 cm front to back and 56 cm wide, centred 20 cm forward on the centre line. (4) On it, a plastic comb rack (two rails 1.6 cm wide and 6 mm tall with an 11 mm slot between them, running sideways, 22 cm long) holding a black hard-plastic barber comb on edge, its flat side facing forward and 5 mm down in the slot: 20 cm long, 3 cm deep, 30 g; its toothed part 12 cm long and 3 mm thick (in simulation a plate the hair passes through), centred 20 cm forward and 13 cm left, then a handle 8 cm long and 1 cm thick toward the left. (5) A grey plastic holder block 8 cm front to back, 6 cm wide and 10 cm tall, centred 20 cm forward and 23 cm right, and lying on it a hair clipper, switched on, with no guard: a plastic body 10 cm long, 4.5 cm wide and 2.5 cm tall, 200 g, its steel blade across the front end, pointing forward.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. A tuft's length is how far it reaches from its root when held straight out from the scalp (a ruler in a real trial). Hair is cut where the clipper's blade passes through it: if the comb is in that tuft nearer the scalp than the blade, the tuft is cut to the blade's distance from the scalp, never shorter than the comb's back (the teeth shield the hair inside them); if not, the hair lies flat under the clipper, which shaves it to 1 mm where the blade passes within 6 mm of the scalp and otherwise leaves it. A cut can't be undone. Each tuft earns 1 when it is right (from 2 mm shorter to 3 mm longer than its row's length: 8, 12, 16, 22 mm, bottom to top), 0.25 when it is cut (at least 1 mm shorter than 35 mm) but still too long, and 0 when uncut or too short. The comb is back when it rests in or beside its rack (centre within 3 cm of its start sideways, no more than 1 cm higher); the clipper when it lies flat (within 20 degrees) on its holder or beside it (centre within 6 cm of its start sideways, no more than 1 cm higher). 0.0 once any tuft is under 5 mm (a bald patch), or once the comb or the clipper touches an ear pad (in simulation: comes within 1 cm of it). Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 when all 12 tufts are right and both tools are back; else 0.9 x the average of the 12 tufts' credits (0 to 0.9, rounded to 0.001). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Cut hair can't be restored: each trial needs a training head with fresh hair, trimmed to 35 mm at the twelve marked locks. Stand the comb back in its rack and lay the clipper, switched on, back on its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Hair is not simulated: each lock is drawn, nothing collides with it, and it hangs unless the comb is in it. A lock is cut where the clipper's blade face crosses its straight-out line if the comb crosses it nearer the scalp; with no comb, the blade shaves it to 1 mm within 6 mm of the scalp, else passes over. The clipper runs throughout. The head is stacked cylinders, so its curve is stepped.
